T: Cook what you love. Load up the truck.
D: A top chef quits his restaurant after a viral meltdown and starts again with a food truck.
P: Serve the toasties when Carl makes his son a grilled cheese.
S: the scene where Carl makes his son a toastie
Thick white bread buttered on the outside, filled with sharp cheddar, gruyère and a little parmesan, cooked slowly in a pan over low heat, lid on, until the cheese pours, cut on the diagonal.
Yuca peeled, boiled 20 minutes until tender, cut into batons, fried at 185C until crisp, salted, with a garlic and lime mojo.
New Orleans beignets with chicory café
the road trip stop in New Orleans

Pillowy yeasted squares fried until puffed and golden, buried under icing sugar, with a jug of hot café au lait for dunking. Mix 7g yeast, 50g sugar and 180ml warm water, then add 80ml evaporated milk, 1 egg, 30g melted butter and 400g plain flour. Knead briefly, cover and chill overnight. Roll to 5mm, cut into 6cm squares and rest 20 minutes. Fry at 180C for 1 minute a side until puffed. Bury in 100g icing sugar. Serve with 500ml strong coffee mixed with 500ml hot milk.
M: Pork shoulder marinated in mojo of orange, lime, garlic and oregano, roasted at 160C for 4 hours, sliced, layered in a soft roll with ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard, pressed and griddled in butter.
the late-night pasta Carl cooks for Molly

Spaghetti tossed with golden sliced garlic, chilli flakes, parsley, lemon and good olive oil, emulsified with starchy pasta water until glossy. Boil 500g spaghetti in well salted water until just al dente, keeping a cup of pasta water. Meanwhile, warm 125ml olive oil with 8 thinly sliced garlic cloves over low heat for 5 minutes until just golden, then add 1 tsp chilli flakes. Toss the spaghetti in the pan with 125ml pasta water until glossy. Finish with a big handful of chopped parsley, lemon zest and a squeeze of lemon.
W: the dessert the critic tears apart, done right
Dark chocolate and butter melted, whisked into eggs and sugar, a little flour folded in, baked in buttered ramekins at 220C for 9 minutes so the centre runs.
K: a Miami summer on the truck
Mint and lime muddled with sugar, 45ml white rum, crushed ice, topped with soda.

s.note: the scene where Carl makes his son a toastie
s.how: Butter the outside of 8 slices white bread. Fill with 150g vintage cheddar, 80g gruyère and a little parmesan. Cook slowly in a pan over low heat with a lid on until the cheese pours. Cut on the diagonal.

Peel 1kg cassava and boil for 20 minutes until tender. Cut into batons and fry at 185C until crisp, then salt. Mix 3 crushed garlic cloves with the juice of a lime and an orange and 3 tbsp oil for mojo.

m.how: Marinate 1kg pork shoulder in the juice of 2 oranges and 2 limes, 4 garlic cloves and oregano overnight. Roast at 160C for 4 hours and slice. Layer in 4 soft rolls with 150g ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard. Press and griddle in butter.

w.note: the dessert the critic tears apart, done right
w.how: Melt 125g dark chocolate with 125g butter. Whisk 2 eggs and 2 yolks with 60g sugar, combine and fold in 30g flour. Bake in 4 buttered ramekins at 220C for 9 minutes so the centre runs. Turn out with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: a Miami summer on the truck
d.how: For each drink, muddle 8 mint leaves with half a lime and 2 tsp sugar. Add 45ml white rum and crushed ice, then top with soda water. Stir from the bottom. Makes four.
